Topology audit

Orbital view: x is each satellite's own ascending-node longitude and y its argument of latitude (0–360°, Earth-fixed axes at t = 0), from its positions 60 s apart; no plane or slot snapping. Ground sites are projected onto northbound/southbound positions for each represented inclination family where an overhead pass is geometrically possible. Dashed lines wrap across the periodic plot edges.

ISLs are modeled fixed graphs: Hypatia's ideal torus, pinned OCM version-budget matching, or geometry-limited GP catalog models. These are not observed operational links. Map lines join sub-satellite positions, not ground cables.

3D uses the recorded Earth-fixed satellite coordinates in kilometers and a WGS84 reference ellipsoid. Drag to rotate, scroll to zoom, right drag to pan. Pink segments are the selected route; they do not represent observed operational ISLs. No playback or interpolation is applied.

Gateways do not relay traffic: a route ends at its fixed registered destination or its first eligible anycast gateway.

Radius counts physical links from the serving satellite: ISLs plus the satellite-to-gateway link. User access and the virtual outlet are excluded.

Users sampled inside explicit Available Now residential coverage polygons dated April 9, 2024; this is historical coverage. Gateway deployment and coordinate uncertainty are documented in the downloadable source audit. Land outlines: Natural Earth, public domain; used only as display context. Shell selections load processed JSON from this static site; no runtime external API or map service is used.
